title: Workload Conservatory — continuous advisor for batching & prefix caching
creator: Diego Ramos
description:
Problem: customers pay a large fraction of inference spend to suboptimal per-request batching and redundant prefix computation. We need an automated advisor that profiles live workloads, suggests batching and KV cache policies, and applies changes safely with observable rollbacks.

Scope: build 'Workload Conservatory' — a continuous recommendation engine that: (1) profiles requests (latency, sequence length, prefix reuse, arrival distribution) across model routes, (2) synthesizes heuristic-safe batching parameters and cache-key rules, (3) exposes explainable suggestions to Console and API, and (4) supports a staged apply/rollback pipeline with automated safety gates.

Out of scope: model retraining, tokenization changes, pricing engine changes. This ticket covers recommender logic, telemetry, and safe apply automation for hosted/Dedicated routes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Advisor produces candidate batching and prefix-KV cache configurations per route with expected cost delta estimate and confidence score. 2) Console shows explanation and a one-click 'simulate' that runs in shadow for 24h. 3) Safe-apply pipeline can deploy changes to a canary subset, monitor defined metrics, and auto-rollback on breach. 4) End-to-end tests and a canary run reduce per-token spend by >=6% on at least two internal workloads with <5% p95 latency regression.

rollout_plan:
1) Shadow simulation (24-72h) with full telemetry and cost-estimation enabled. 2) Canary apply to 3% of production routes (by route tag), monitor 12h windows with automated SLO checks. 3) Ramp to 10%/30%/100% over 24-48h increments if metrics stable. 4) Post-ramp analysis (7 days) and feedback loop to heuristics.

Gates: auto-rollback triggers include p95 latency increase >5% absolute or error-rate increase >0.5% (absolute), or observed cost delta worse than predicted by >10%.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback via config service: revert advisor-applied config and re-issue route restartless update. If rollback fails, fallback to runtime safe-mode which pins batch size to 1 and disables prefix caching for the affected route. Runbook steps: (a) notify on-call, (b) open incident, (c) revert via console or API, (d) validate metrics within 15 minutes.
notes: Tradeoffs considered: ML-based recommender (higher accuracy, longer iteration) vs heuristic rule engine (explainable, faster, easier safety properties). We chose heuristics + supervised feedback loop for first delivery to minimize risk and enable human review. Future iteration: ML ranking model trained on shadow outcomes.
